Now, just a quick reminder about that transverse signal we measure.  We apply the RF pulse at the Larmor frequency, and the spin together (coherently) for some time, but they become less coherent over time.  That is the T2 decay.

## The FID signal 

![K-space.](images/ch17/k-space.png){#fig-ch17-k-space}
As the spins rotate their impact on the coil varies, driving the voltage up and down to create the oscillation we measure.

## The gradient and the spins

<!--
## Initial insight: Magnetic gradients produce different temporal signals

![Initial insight: Magnetic gradients produce different temporal signals.](images/ch17/initial-insight-magnetic-gradients-produce-differe.png){#fig-ch17-initial-insight-magnetic-gradients-produce-differe}
-->

![New insight: Spatial gradients produce different spatial weightings.](images/ch17/new-insight-spatial-gradients-produce-different-sp.png){#fig-ch17-new-insight-spatial-gradients-produce-different-sp}

Two locations, at different magnetic field levels, will spin at different Larmor frequencies.  As a result, they might start out together, but one might be spinning faster (blue) than the other (pink).  So one might be in a positive orientation while the other is in a negative orientation.

<!--
![Gradients control spin orientations across space.](images/ch17/gradients-control-spin-orientations-across-space.png){#fig-ch17-gradients-control-spin-orientations-across-space}
-->

## Summing signals across space

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![MRI X gradient: spatially varying spin orientations produce a spatial harmonic.](images/ch17/MRI_X%20Gradient.mp4){#vid-ch17-mri-x-gradient width="70%" loop="true" autoplay="true" muted="true"}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![MRI X gradient: spatially varying spin orientations produce a spatial harmonic (video; see the HTML version for the animation).](images/ch17/gradients-control-spin-orientations-across-space.png){#vid-ch17-mri-x-gradient width="70%"}
:::

This video illustrates the impact of applying an imaging gradient on the spins.

Notice that the spin orientations change with respect to one another systematically.  Each is rotating at its own Larmor frequency. Because the frequencies differ, we introduce a pattern of orientations across space.  The pattern is a spatial harmonic.  Each column contributes to the overall signal, therefore, differently.  Some contribute negatively (they are pointing away from the coil) and others positively (they are pointing towards the coil).

## Visualing oscillations: pendula

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![The pendula are swinging at a range of temporal frequencies.](images/ch17/Pendula-MR-Gradients.mov){#vid-ch17-pendula-mr-gradients width="70%" loop="true" autoplay="true" muted="true"}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![The pendula are swinging at a range of temporal frequencies (video; see the HTML version for the animation).](images/ch17/the-pendula-are-swinging-at-a-range-of-temporal-fr.png){#vid-ch17-pendula-mr-gradients width="70%"}
:::

I like this visualization the spatial pattern that arises from different temporal frequencies. 

The balls are oscillating at different frequencies because the string lengths differ. Over time, they spatial pattern across the balls differs, because their frequency of oscillation differ. 

This visualization, like the movie, shows the weighting **across space**.  The spatial pattern is a sinusoid because the temporal patterns are sinusoidal oscillations.

## The magnetization is weighted by different spatial harmonics

And it is so important, that I illustrate the spatial weighting once more, this time with a fancier graphic.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Time 1

![Fourier encoding:  the magnetization is weighted by different spatial harmonics — step 1.](images/ch17/fourier-encoding-the-magnetization-is-weighted-by-1.png){#fig-ch17-fourier-encoding-the-magnetization-is-weighted-by-1}

## Time 2

![Fourier encoding:  the magnetization is weighted by different spatial harmonics — step 2.](images/ch17/fourier-encoding-the-magnetization-is-weighted-by-2.png){#fig-ch17-fourier-encoding-the-magnetization-is-weighted-by-2}

## Time 3

![Fourier encoding:  the magnetization is weighted by different spatial harmonics — step 3.](images/ch17/fourier-encoding-the-magnetization-is-weighted-by-3.png){#fig-ch17-fourier-encoding-the-magnetization-is-weighted-by-3}

:::

These images show that we measure the weighted sum of the signals across space.  The weighting applied across space is a harmonic because the spins are oscillating at their own respective Larmor frequencies.  

And what is the size of the signal from each location?  That is the size of the FID at that location.  So we are measuring the spatial sum of all the FID signals, weighted by a harmonic across space.  

::: {.callout-note title="Check your intuition"}
The picture of the harmonic across the brain slice times the image of the brain slice matches one of the mathematical ideas in the section on Fourier Series (@sec-fourier-series).  Try to connect the two in your mind.  Ask me about it in class.
:::
